confidence_notes: I used web searches of aggregated cost-of-living indexes (Numbeo, CityCost, Expatistan) to set the food and drink anchors. Those sources gave ringgit prices of about RM15 for an inexpensive meal, about RM80 for a mid-range meal for two, about RM12 for a cappuccino and about RM17 for a domestic draft pint. I converted them at about 4.08 MYR per USD, the rate implied by CityCost's own USD/MYR pairs. That rate is approximate, and these are current late-2026 aggregate prices, not prices specific to July 2026. Beer prices vary widely (RM10-30). I set a standard serving slightly below the pint figure. Malaysia's high alcohol excise makes drinks expensive compared with food. Cocktail and wine anchors are less certain. I found no aggregated per-glass wine price, and the cocktail data came only from individual venues (roughly 8-10 in an unstated currency) and general bar spending ranges (about RM30-50). So I estimated these from the local markup over beer, at about 2.3x for cocktails and 1.9x for wine. All four accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge, not from searches or listings. They assume normal George Town tourist demand in July and have the lowest certainty. The FX observation comes from a web search summary of RBA data, not from reading the RBA page directly.
comparable_city_reasoning: Food prices come straight from Penang aggregate indexes. Accommodation is benchmarked against Malaysian and Southeast Asian heritage tourist cities such as Melaka and Chiang Mai, and is slightly below Kuala Lumpur. Drink prices reflect Malaysia's high alcohol duties and are above Thai or Vietnamese levels.
